As written, (landau_weak3) is the time-reversed, entropy-increasing equation: choosing phi = log f yields dH/dt = +1/2 double-integral |tilde-nabla log f|^2 f f_* >= 0. The same sign slip makes the displayed derivation 'Then (dL-new) directly follows from (dL)' false as written: substituting V = tilde-nabla phi into the constraint of (dL) yields weak dynamics +1/2 double-integral (nabla phi - nabla_* phi_*) . A (u-u_*) f f_*, while the constraint of (dL-new) yields -1/2 of the same expression; consistency requires V = -tilde-nabla phi (or an overall sign change of the continuity equation).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip a single sign in the formalism, e.g. define the divergence in (new_div) with the opposite sign, or equivalently put a minus sign in (landau_weak3) and in the constraint of (dL), so that (0910), (landau_weak3), (dL) and (dL-new) become mutually consistent; no mathematical content changes.

Nothing downstream is damaged: d_L is unchanged because its infimum over V is sign-invariant, and the dynamical JKO problem (djko), its optimality conditions (opt_u)-(opt_u1), and the resulting scheme are derived independently with mutually consistent signs.
issues.title: Sign inconsistency between (0910)/(new_div) and (landau_weak3), and between (dL) and (dL-new)
issues.why_classification: A one-sign local correction restores full consistency; every substantive claim (the Landau metric, the gradient-flow structure, the JKO scheme and its stated properties) is preserved with no new argument, no reoptimization, and no loss of scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: If $\varphi(\bv) : \R^d \to \R^d$ satisfies $\int_{\R^d} A(\bv-\bv_*) (\varphi -\varphi_*)f_* \rd\bv_* = 0$, then $\varphi \in \text{span}\{ \mathbf{1}, \bv\}$ on the support of $f$.
Since $A$ is semi-positive definite, this implies $A(\bv-\bv_*)(\varphi -\varphi_*) = 0$ on the support of $f_* f$.

issues.failure_explanation: From the premise the proof only obtains A(v-v_*)(phi(v)-phi(v_*)) = 0 on supp(f f_*), i.e. phi(v)-phi(v_*) is parallel to v-v_* for all v, v_* in supp f. The concluding implication to affine form with a scalar slope is asserted with no argument, and it is false as stated for degenerate supports (the paper explicitly does not distinguish probability measures from densities): if supp f is contained in a line {v0 + s e}, any phi of the form phi(v0+se) = a + lambda(s) e with arbitrary (e.g. nonlinear) lambda satisfies the premise but does not belong to span{1, v}. A hypothesis excluding collinear support, together with the standard short argument that pointwise parallelism on a non-collinear set forces phi(v) = a + b v with scalar b, is required.

failure_location.quote: Therefore, $\varphi \in span\{ \mathbf{1}, \bv\}$ on the support of $f$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that supp f is not contained in a line (or has nonempty interior) and insert the standard few-line rigidity argument; the lemma's use and all downstream conclusions are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma 1 as stated is false in the collinear-support case and its proof is incomplete; its application to the optimality condition (opt_u) in the JKO first-order consistency analysis (densities with full support) is unaffected.
issues.title: Lemma 1: missing support-nondegeneracy hypothesis and missing rigidity argument in the proof
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard local condition plus a routine short argument repairs the statement with no change to any conclusion, method, rate, or advertised scope.

issues.failure_explanation: The final inequality of the proof bounds (1/(BN)) sum_q sum_{(i,j) in C_q} ||grad ell(theta_k) - grad ell_{i,j}(theta_{q-1})||^2 solely by (L^2 B/N) sum_q ||theta_k - theta_{q-1}||^2. This is invalid: grad ell(theta_k) - grad ell_{i,j}(theta_{q-1}) does not vanish when theta_{q-1} = theta_k, and because Algorithm algorithm_opt sums only over within-batch pairs (NB of the N^2 pairs per epoch), the per-epoch sum does not telescope to the full gradient even at a fixed iterate, so a component-variance term ||grad ell(theta_k) - grad ell_{i,j}(theta_k)||^2 (controlled only via assumption (A.3)) is indispensable. Concrete failure: in one dimension with N = 2, B = 1, ell_{i,j}(theta) = c_{i,j} theta + theta^2/2 and (c_{11}, c_{12}, c_{21}, c_{22}) = (-1, 3, 3, -1), one has grad ell(0) = 1 while both within-batch component gradients equal -1; the epoch moves theta_k = 0 to approximately +alpha and ell increases by approximately alpha, whereas the lemma asserts a decrease of approximately -alpha/2 for small alpha. Hence sgd_lemma2 is false as stated and the proof of Theorem thm_opt_conv breaks. Moreover the theorem's neighborhood 6 sigma^2 L^2 alpha^2 N/B^2 = O(alpha^2 sigma^2) is unattainable for this estimator: the batch-pair gradient has O(sigma^2) variance at the current iterate, so any correct constant-step analysis yields an O(alpha sigma^2)-order neighborhood, one factor of alpha worse.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Carry the variance term through the descent estimate (e.g. via ||grad ell(theta_k) - grad ell_{i,j}(theta_{q-1})||^2 <= 2 L^2 ||theta_k - theta_{q-1}||^2 + 2 ||grad ell(theta_k) - grad ell_{i,j}(theta_k)||^2, then take expectations and apply (A.3)), re-telescope with the resulting O(alpha sigma^2)-type neighborhood (and any needed smallness condition on M), and restate Theorem thm_opt_conv with the corrected bound.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma sgd_lemma2 and Theorem thm_opt_conv are invalid as stated; the convergence guarantee advertised for Algorithm algorithm_opt (and echoed in the introduction's 'convergence analysis under common optimization theory assumptions') is not established, and the stated error floor overstates the achievable rate by a factor of alpha.
issues.title: Descent lemma for reshuffled double-sum SGD drops the within-batch-pair sampling variance, invalidating Theorem thm_opt_conv's O(alpha^2 sigma^2) floor
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained reanalysis of Section 4.2 that produces a standard, recognizably comparable SGD-type guarantee (convergence to a neighborhood that still vanishes as alpha tends to 0, but at a weaker rate in alpha and possibly under extra hypotheses); the stated bound cannot be kept, yet no new global proof architecture is needed and the numerical scheme and experiments are unaffected.
